why: Minimise the maximum chosen value: if a capability c allows count non-adjacent picks, any larger c does too. The feasibility check is a greedy scan, take every value <= c whose left neighbour was not taken, which is what makes this a binary search on the answer and not a DP.
hints: Fix a capability c: only values <= c may be picked. Can you then pick count of them with no two adjacent?

Greedy: scan left to right and take a position whenever its value is <= c and the previous position was not taken; taking the earliest allowed position never blocks more than skipping it would. More allowed values can only help, so feasibility is monotone in c.
Binary search c over [min(values), max(values)] (or over the sorted distinct values) for the smallest feasible one. O(n log max).
pitfalls: After taking position i, jump to i + 2.
A max-of-chosen DP per candidate is unnecessary; the greedy is exact.
